neighbours.label: the word-initial fragment ' im' when the tokenizer splits a word after it (im|itate, im|printed, im|poster); single-token im- words stay quiet
fire: The young singer imitated her favorite star so well that the audience gasped.
Each page was imprinted with the seal of the royal library in red ink.
My little brother imitates every move I make, which drives me crazy.
Talented imitators of the famous painter flooded the market with fakes.
In the old tale, mischievous imps hid the farmer's tools every night.
Mockingbirds are skilled at imitating car alarms and ringing phones.
Police said the imposter had used a fake uniform to enter the building.
Collectors pay high prices for rare imprints from small colonial presses.
quiet: The young singer copied her favorite star so well that the audience gasped.
The diamond turned out to be a cheap imitation sold at a market stall.
Each book carries the imprint of the royal library on its spine.
Police said the impostors had used fake uniforms to enter the building.
Her brother is still too immature to share his toys with anyone.
The trade imbalance between the two countries grew again last year.
The painter's early work was imperfect but surprisingly impressive.
Mockingbirds are skilled at copying car alarms and ringing phones.

notes: Probe: split ' im' words scored 0.48-0.70 of max, single-token 'imitation' 0.006. Near misses keep the im- meaning (imitation, imprint, impostors = 'impost'+'ors') but without the bare ' im' piece.
